answer: Unique-task proof-of-work. Each identity must solve a challenge derived from its own declared task, and the solution must include a cipher keyed to that task's inputs so no two agents can submit the same answer. Duplicate solutions collapse to one identity, while near-duplicates fail validation. To farm N identities, an attacker must generate N genuinely distinct tasks and solve each independently, paying full compute per identity rather than amortizing one answer. The garden of valid tasks stays open but non-fungible; a single yarrow-stalk draw cannot seed two claims.
